title: HELIX Bridge: Workday Student → Student
description: Maps Workday Student business objects to the HELIX Student resource. Workday is cloud-native; data is accessed via RaaS (Report-as-a-Service), Workday REST API, or Prism Analytics rather than direct database tables.
architecture_notes: Workday Student uses a unified person model shared with HCM. A student is a 'Person' with a 'Student' role. Data is extracted via: (1) RaaS custom reports exposed as REST endpoints, (2) Workday REST API /students endpoint, (3) Prism Analytics datasets for bulk/lake ingestion, (4) Workday Data Cloud zero-copy integration with AWS (announced June 2026) for direct governed access without ETL.

source_objects.description: Core person record. Unified across HCM and Student. Contains name, demographics, contact info.
Student role on a Person. Contains student-specific attributes, academic status, programs.
Student's relationship to an academic unit. Status, level, class standing.
External IDs (student ID, national ID, etc.) assigned to a person.

attribute_mappings.notes: Every Workday object has a unique WID (Workday ID). Use the Person WID as the stable key.

attribute_mappings.transformation: Direct map. The WID is Workday's internal globally unique identifier.
Direct map. The institution-assigned student ID, configured as a Universal Identifier type in Workday.
attribute_mappings.notes: Workday allows multiple ID types per person. Filter by ID Type = 'Student_ID' or the institution's configured equivalent.

attribute_mappings.transformation: Direct map. Use the 'Legal' name type (Usage_Type = 'Legal').
Use the Preferred name type if configured; null otherwise.
attribute_mappings.notes: Workday natively supports preferred name as a separate name record with Usage_Type = 'Preferred'.

attribute_mappings.transformation: Map Workday gender reference IDs to HELIX: 'Male'→'male', 'Female'→'female', 'Not_Declared'→'unknown'. Workday supports configurable gender identity options.
attribute_mappings.notes: Workday tenants may have custom gender identity values configured. Map the reference ID, not the display label.

attribute_mappings.transformation: Map Workday academic status to HELIX: 'Active'→'enrolled', 'Inactive'→'withdrawn', 'Graduated'→'graduated', 'Leave_of_Absence'→'leave_of_absence', 'Admitted'→'admitted'. Use the current (most recent effective-dated) affiliation.
attribute_mappings.notes: Workday tracks status at the Academic Affiliation level. A student may have multiple affiliations (undergrad, grad). Use the primary or most recent.

attribute_mappings.transformation: Map Workday residency values to HELIX enum. Workday residency is often tied to fee assessment.
attribute_mappings.notes: Residency in Workday Student is configurable per tenant. Common values: 'In_State', 'Out_of_State', 'International'.

attribute_mappings.transformation: Map Workday country reference ID to ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Workday uses ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 internally (e.g., 'USA'→'US').
Map: true/false. Implementation depends on institutional configuration.
attribute_mappings.notes: No standard Workday field for first-generation. Typically captured via a custom object or student recruiting data.

attribute_mappings.transformation: Use the most recent modification timestamp across source objects

extraction_methods.description: Build a custom report in Workday Report Writer that joins Person + Student + Academic Affiliation objects. Expose as a REST endpoint. Supports JSON, CSV, XML output. Ideal for scheduled incremental extracts.
extraction_methods.notes: Most common extraction method for Workday Student data today.

extraction_methods.description: Use the /students resource from Workday's Student REST API (v1+). Returns JSON. Supports paging and field selection. Good for real-time integration.
extraction_methods.notes: Requires API Client configuration and OAuth 2.0 setup in Workday.

extraction_methods.description: Export datasets from Prism Analytics for bulk ingestion into a data lake. Prism can combine Workday data with external sources.
extraction_methods.notes: Good for analytics-first use cases but adds a layer of abstraction.

extraction_methods.description: Announced June 2026. Bi-directional zero-copy access to Workday's governed data layer directly from AWS services (Athena, Redshift, SageMaker). No ETL pipeline required. Data stays governed in Workday.
extraction_methods.notes: Early access as of mid-2026, GA expected later in 2026. This is the most HELIX-aligned extraction path — governed data, no movement, lake-ready.
